result.summary: Extends `-ipcbind` with an optional per-listener `,max-connections=<n>` socket option (defaulting to 16, capped at 256) and URL-decodes Unix socket paths to allow commas in filenames. Incorporates IPC listener sockets and per-listener connection limits into startup file descriptor reservation checks in `init.cpp`. Passes connection caps down to the multiprocess Cap'n Proto listener to stop accepting incoming connections when full.
result.problem: Currently, IPC listeners do not enforce connection limits and are omitted from initialization file descriptor reservation accounting, leaving the daemon vulnerable to file descriptor exhaustion from IPC connections. Furthermore, a proposed global `-ipcmaxconnections` option would not allow different connection caps across separate bind endpoints.
evidence: PR description: "A global option would not allow different limits for different `-ipcbind` addresses, and the inline option format can be extended in the future with additional options."

Commit 3d2b65d050: "Reserve file descriptors for each configured -ipcbind listener and its default connection slots during initialization. Cap IPC reservations conservatively so downstream int-based file descriptor accounting cannot overflow."
result.scope_notes: Adds `src/ipc/listen.cpp` for parsing socket options on Unix socket addresses, and introduces a new functional test `test/functional/interface_ipc_init.py`.
result.changed_since_previous: No substantial changes to the approach or diff; commits remain focused on per-listener socket option parsing, file descriptor reservation during init, and test coverage.
result.card: PR #35037 adds per-listener connection limits to `-ipcbind` using inline options (e.g. `-ipcbind=unix:/custom/path,max-connections=8`, default 16, max 256). It incorporates IPC listeners and connection slots into node initialization file descriptor calculations to prevent file descriptor exhaustion. This provides a flexible per-endpoint alternative to the global limit proposed in PR #34978.

risk.why: Mistakes in option parsing or startup IPC file descriptor calculations could prevent nodes from starting when -ipcbind is configured.
